extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Patent Office examiners and patent practitioners handling reissue applications
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive requirements for examination, public notice/access, handling of litigation, and oath/declaration/ownership matters for U.S. patent reissue applications under MPEP and 37 CFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette notice and identifying data
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of all reissue applications, except CPAs filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d), will be announced in the Official Gazette and will include certain identifying data as specified in 37 CFR 1.11(b) (filing date, reissue and original patent numbers, title, class and subclass, name of inventor, owner of record, attorney/agent of record, and Examining Group).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement should be done prior to any examination. If publication was inadvertently omitted, action should be taken to publish as quickly as possible and examination may be delayed until two months after publication to allow protests. For 08/earlier series, the 'REISSUE' tag and PALM screen (2952) / 09 series face of file wrapper are sources to verify publication date. If not announced, return to Office of Initial Patent Examination to handle announcement and do not act on the reissue until 2 months after announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.11(b) provides that all reissue applications filed after March 1, 1977 are open to inspection by the general public, and copies may be furnished upon paying the fee therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any member of the public may request access to a particular reissue application; an oral request suffices (no record intended to be kept). Reissue files will be maintained in the Examining Groups and inspection supervised by Group personnel. A Group Director or appropriate Office official may, under appropriate circumstances, postpone access or copying (e.g., to avoid interruption of examination). Requests for copies must be in writing and addressed to the Commissioner and fees charged per 37 CFR 1.19. CPAs of reissue applications will not be announced in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-month delay before examiner action (special handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for reissue will be acted on by the examiner in advance of other applications (taken up 'special'), but not sooner than two months after announcement of the filing of the reissue application has appeared in the Official Gazette (37 CFR 1.176).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two-month delay allows the public to submit protests under 37 CFR 1.291(a). The Office may entertain petitions under 37 CFR 1.183 (with fee under 1.17(h)) to waive the delay; protests filed after the two months may still be considered if timely under relevant rules. Reissue applications with related litigation will be acted on before other special applications and may be acted on immediately subject to the 2-month delay after publication unless waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of re-presented original claims
rubrics_metrics.description: An original claim, if re-presented in the reissue application, is subject to reexamination, and the entire application will be examined in the same manner as original applications, subject to the rules relating thereto, except that division will not be required (37 CFR 1.176).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-presented claims and the entire reissue application are to be fully examined as if being presented for the first time; reissue applications are normally examined by the same examiner who issued the patent. Examiner should review compliance with 37 CFR 1.171-1.179 and ensure the reissue oath/declaration complies with 1.175 (see MPEP §1444). The original patent file wrapper should always be ordered and reviewed when examining a reissue application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue oath/declaration substantive requirements (37 CFR 1.175)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue oath/declaration must include: (A) a statement that the applicant believes the original patent to be wholly or partly inoperative or invalid (by defective specification/drawing or by claiming more or less than right to claim); (B) a statement of at least one error relied upon to support the reissue application; (C) a statement that all errors being corrected arose without deceptive intention; and (D) the information required by 37 CFR 1.63.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP §1414 discusses each element and examiners should carefully review the oath/declaration for compliance. If the oath/declaration is insufficient, the examiner should reject all claims under 35 U.S.C. 251 and use form paragraphs (e.g., 14.01–14.01.04) to state defects, followed by paragraph 14.14 to reject claims under 35 U.S.C. 251.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of defective or missing reissue oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the initial reissue oath/declaration fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.175 (e.g., lacks an error statement or identifies no proper error), the examiner should reject all claims as based upon a defective reissue oath/declaration under 35 U.S.C. 251 and require a supplemental reissue oath/declaration in reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the initial oath/declaration properly identified an error but later amendments remove reliance on that error, a supplemental oath/declaration identifying at least one error currently relied upon is required (but may be deferred until condition for allowance if prior oath was proper). A supplemental oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.175(b)(1) must be submitted before allowance and will be required where (A) application is otherwise in condition for allowance, (B) amendments/corrections made are subsequent to last oath, and (C) at least one amendment corrects an error under 35 U.S.C. 251.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain of title and consent documentary evidence (37 CFR 1.172)
rubrics_metrics.description: On initial receipt, the examiner should inspect the submission under 37 CFR 1.172 as to documentary evidence of a chain of title from the original owner to the assignee to determine whether the consent requirement of 37 CFR 1.172 has been met; the assignee indicated by the documentary evidence must be the same assignee which signed the consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare consent and documentary evidence of ownership; the persons signing consent and evidence must have authority. If assigned and no submission under 1.172 is present, require submission using form paragraph 14.16. If statement of record indicates the application is not assigned, no documentary evidence under 1.172 should be required. See MPEP §324 and §1410.01 for further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify patent term/maintenance and incorporation of certificate of correction
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should verify that the patent on which the reissue application is based has not expired due to term run or failure to pay maintenance fees; also verify that all Certificate of Correction changes have been properly incorporated into the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a patent has expired, the Commissioner no longer has authority under 35 U.S.C. 251 to reissue the patent (see In re Morgan). Require compliance regarding surrender of original patent or affidavit of loss in first office action if not provided. See MPEP §§1415.01, 1411.01, and 1416 for handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and handling of litigation related to reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent sought to be reissued is involved in litigation, the existence and details of such litigation that are material to patentability must be brought to the Office's attention at or shortly after filing, preferably in the reissue oath/declaration or separate paper; litigation begun after filing should be promptly reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit details and documents material to patentability (defenses against validity usually material). Examiner should determine whether the original patent has been adjudicated and may request STIC litigation search; place prominent notation on application file indicating litigation and on the pink Reissue Notice Card. If litigation details are not of record, the examiner should inquire in the next Office action (form paragraph 14.06). If additional details appear material, examiner may make further inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension/stay rules where concurrent litigation exists
rubrics_metrics.description: Action in reissue applications with indication of concurrent litigation will be suspended automatically unless (A) a stay of the litigation is in effect; (B) the litigation has been terminated; (C) there are no significant overlapping issues between the application and the litigation; or (D) applicant desires examination at that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of (A)-(D) apply, use form paragraphs 14.08–14.10 to deny suspension. Where none apply, suspend action using form paragraph 14.11. Examiner should consult Group Special Program Examiner prior to suspending. Reissue applications with stayed litigation are to be expedited and taken up 'special'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply periods and extensions during litigation-related reissue prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants will normally be given 1 month to reply to Office actions in reissue applications being examined during litigation; this 1-month period may be extended only upon a showing of clear justification pursuant to 37 CFR 1.136(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions of 37 CFR 1.136(a) (extensions under 1.136(a)) will not be permitted during prosecution of litigation-related reissue applications; up to 3 months may be set for reply if examiner determines such period clearly justified. Office actions should inform applicant that 1.136(a) is not available. Time-monitoring systems and monthly reports are required for reissue applications related to litigation; Group Special Program Examiner oversees related litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of protests and public submissions for reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Public submissions pertinent to patentability may be submitted in the form of a protest under 37 CFR 1.291(a). The public should file submissions as early as possible; protests submitted after the 2-month delay may still be considered under timeliness/content criteria in MPEP §1901.04 and §1901.06.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests filed after two months need not be accompanied by petitions under 1.182 or 1.183 unless a final rejection has been issued or prosecution on the merits has been closed. Once the first Office action is mailed, a protest may still be submitted and will be considered in the next Office action as appropriate. See MPEP §1901.06 for examiner procedures on protests in reissue applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special status of reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: All reissue applications are taken up 'special,' and remain 'special' even though applicant does not respond promptly; all reissue applications, except those under suspension because of litigation, will be taken up for action ahead of other 'special' applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This means all issues not deferred will be treated and responded to immediately. Reissue applications involved in litigation or stayed litigation will be processed with great emphasis on expedited handling; petitions may be entertained to waive the 2-month delay under appropriate circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merged reexamination/reissue proceedings rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reissue application has been merged with a reexamination proceeding, the merged proceeding generally will not be stayed where there is litigation; in a merged reexamination/reissue proceeding, the reexamination will control because of 35 U.S.C. 305 requirement for special dispatch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§2285 and 2286 for merged proceeding handling; examiners should be aware that reexamination statutory obligations may supersede ordinary reissue suspension practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record-keeping and file updates for reissue notices (PTO-445)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application for a reissue is filed, a Form PTO-445 notice is placed in the file of the original patent identifying the reissue application by application number and filing date. When the reissue is granted or otherwise terminated, the fact will be added to the notice in the original patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When divisional or continuation reissue applications are filed, a separate form is placed in the original patent file for each reissue. When the reissue issues, Examining Group technical support must inform File Information Unit (Record Room) by memo so that Form PTO-445 can be updated. The Examining Group indicated in the Official Gazette should retain the reissue file for two months before transferring it under MPEP §903.08(d).
